record.paper_title: Phase-type distributions and representations: Some results and open problems for system theory
record.original_question: What is a natural direct counterpart of reachability for phase-type representations? In a phase-type representation, a generator T is called simple when any two distinct initial probability distributions give rise to two distinct phase-type distributions, and this simplicity is close to observability through a rank condition on the matrix [v, Tv, ..., T^(n-1)v]. The problem is to identify the corresponding reachability notion for phase-type representations in a way that has a natural probabilistic, structural, or graph-theoretic interpretation rather than only an indirect dual-time construction.

evidence.quote: Definition 2 (O'Cinneide 1989): A PH generator T is simple if any two initial probability distributions α1 ≠ α2, give rise to two different PH-distributions.
This notion is very close to our observability notion. Up to now, a direct counterpart of reachability is not known.
Problem 4: Give a natural interpretation of the counterpart of reachability for PH-representations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A phase-type (PH) distribution is the distribution of the time until absorption of a continuous-time Markov chain on the state space {1,...,n,n+1}, where state n+1 is absorbing and states 1,...,n are transient. Such a chain is described by a pair (α, T), called a PH-representation, where α is a 1×n row vector of nonnegative entries (the initial probability distribution on the transient states, with α·1 ≤ 1), and T is an n×n subgenerator matrix (off-diagonal entries nonnegative, row sums ≤ 0, and T nonsingular). The associated PH-distribution function is F(t) = 1 − α e^{tT} 1, for t ≥ 0, where 1 is the column vector of ones.

Call the subgenerator T simple if for any two distinct initial probability vectors α₁ ≠ α₂, the resulting PH-distributions are different, i.e. the map α ↦ α e^{tT} 1 is injective in α. Equivalently (setting v = T·1, or equivalently using the column vector 1), simplicity is characterized by the rank condition
   rank [ v, Tv, T²v, …, T^{n−1} v ] = n,
which is the observability-type Kalman rank condition of the linear system (T, 1).

Problem: Provide a notion that is, for PH-representations, the natural counterpart of reachability in linear systems theory — analogous to how simplicity above is the counterpart of observability — and which admits a direct probabilistic, structural, or graph-theoretic interpretation in terms of the underlying Markov chain (i.e., not merely defined indirectly via the time-reversed/dual PH-representation).
artifact.status_search_result: No web evidence indicates that a direct probabilistic/structural counterpart of reachability for PH-representations (beyond the indirect dual-time construction) has been established. The question is stated as an explicit open problem in the literature on PH-representations and system theory, and searches did not return a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Characterizing phase type distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of O'Cinneide's characterization of phase-type distributions and their representations, without resolving a reachability counterpart.
status_evidence.claim: Standard references discuss characterization/representation of PH-distributions but do not provide a direct reachability counterpart to the simplicity/observability notion.

status_evidence.title: A Constructive Proof of the Phase-Type Characterization Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Constructive proof related to PH-representations following O'Cinneide.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to investigate PH-representations without identifying a probabilistic reachability counterpart.
